requirements.requirement: Establish a healthy three-member etcd cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
requirements.summary: No etcd package or binary pre-existed on any node (before_prepare snapshots and cmd-928e09ac84694e43/cmd-e0fa43ce2ea6415b/cmd-d4f58fa194de4e64 show only ssh listening). Executor installed etcd 3.5.17 from upstream binaries on all three nodes and bootstrapped a 3-member cluster; cmd-700a474bc12340ad shows member list with node1/node2/node3 all 'started'. Five /app/* keys were written and endpoint health for all three endpoints reported healthy (cmd-671f3fba966a4abb), and node3's own endpoint independently returned all five keys before any disruption (cmd-322424b258ad4b94), confirming a genuinely replicated healthy baseline.

requirements.requirement: Simulate/represent the node3 member as permanently lost with unrecoverable data
requirements.summary: etcd was stopped and disabled on node3 (cmd-3d55123c718f4f4f), the member was removed from the cluster via the surviving quorum on node1/node2 (cmd-db861f2016a9439e, member list dropping to 2 started members), and node3's data directory was wiped with rm -rf, confirmed empty afterward (cmd-efc450dc989e4d96), making the prior member state irrecoverable exactly as the task describes.

requirements.requirement: Cluster and data remain available on the surviving quorum during the node3 outage
requirements.summary: With node3 stopped, removed, and wiped, the remaining node2 endpoint reported healthy and returned all five original /app/* keys (cmd-07bccd78f7f9478d), directly demonstrating that the 2-member quorum stayed available and consistent during the disruption window.

requirements.requirement: Replace the lost member with a working member on node3, restoring the cluster to three healthy members with existing keys intact
requirements.summary: A new member was added for node3 via `member add` (cmd-d6235041d79448af), node3 was reconfigured with ETCD_INITIAL_CLUSTER_STATE=existing and its etcd service started successfully (cmd-1cb3b18190494263). Post-join verification shows member list with 3 started members, all endpoints healthy, and matching raft term/index across all three nodes (cmd-bb7d083a686844c1), and node3's own endpoint directly returned all five original keys, confirming full data resync (cmd-5739a817fa474172).

overall_summary: The executor built the etcd cluster and its application keys from scratch (nothing pre-existed per the before_prepare snapshot), then faithfully enacted the task's described failure scenario on node3 (stop, remove from cluster, irrecoverable data wipe) while directly demonstrating that the surviving quorum stayed healthy and data-complete throughout. It then added a fresh node3 member with ETCD_INITIAL_CLUSTER_STATE=existing, and directly verified the restored cluster had three started members with matching raft term/index and all five original keys present on every endpoint including node3 itself. All four material outcomes are satisfied with direct, non-conflicting evidence. Independently of the public task, the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with a coherent chain of pre-restart boot id + health, reboot acknowledgement, connection-drop confirmation, a distinct post-restart boot id, and full recovered cluster/data verification; these boot ids are corroborated by the fixed before_prepare/after_executor lifecycle snapshots for all three nodes, adding independent cross-check confidence.
limitations: Leftover installation residue (tarball, extracted directory, start/reboot logs) was left in /tmp on all three nodes rather than cleaned up; low-risk but unaddressed.

Node3's pre-restart boot-identity/health capture for the restart protocol (cmd-f9139291e6944a45) occurred after the member-replacement work rather than at the very start, which is appropriate for the restart protocol's own baseline but means it does not double as evidence of the original pre-disruption node3 boot state (that is separately covered by req-1 evidence).

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all state-changing commands map directly to task-required setup, the required outage simulation, the replacement, or the mandatory restart protocol. All state-changing actions (package install, firewalld service additions, systemd unit/config creation, member remove/add, data wipe, and node reboots) are traceable to a required outcome or the fixed restart protocol, and no failed/conflicting services or unsafe exposure resulted (after_executor failed-services checks are empty on all three nodes). The one recurring minor issue is leftover build residue in /tmp on all three nodes — the downloaded tarball (/tmp/etcd.tar.gz), the extracted etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 directory, and /tmp/etcd_start.log and /tmp/reboot.log were never cleaned up after installation completed (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff for node1, node2, and node3). This is low-risk, bounded residue with no functional or security impact, but it was retained rather than reverted.
